newsitem.title: USA: Vastar sees '96 spending at $575 mln -- CFO.
newsitem.headline: Vastar sees '96 spending at $575 mln -- CFO.

text.p: Vastar Resources Inc, fresh from a successful round of bidding on Gulf of Mexico drilling tracts, said its 1996 exploration and production budget should be $575 million, the company's chief financial officer said.
He declined to project what the company's 1997 budget would be, but noted spending has climbed in the last two years from $440 million in 1995 and $335 million in 1994.

"We are not opportunity-constrained," Steven Shapiro, Vastar CFO told Reuters Friday, noting spending would depend on a number of factors, including natural gas prices. He noted 74 percent of Vastar's drilling portfolio is for natural gas.

Separately, Vastar said Friday it was the apparent successful bidder, solely or with others on 26 tracts in Wednesday's Gulf of Mexico lease sale. Vastar said it would spend about $14 million if all the tracts are awarded.

Shapiro also told Reuters Vastar's plans to begin exploring deep water prospects next year in the Gulf could raise the percentage of crude oil in the company's production portfolio since geological data suggest there is likely to be more crude than natural gas in the Gulf's deep water.
